highlights.text: form a root (aṣl) indicating a certain kind of sound
highlights.note: Ibn Fāris's root sense: a kind of sound

highlights.text: **al-ṣākhkha:** said to be the cry that deafens the ears.
b-kh-l as expressing a single idea: miserliness / stinginess
a line by the poet Ruʾba using bakhkhāl
al-darham and al-dirhim — two dialectal pronunciations of the coin "dirham."
a single core sense: the heart's or mind's repeated turning-over of something
tafakkara — "he reflected," used of one who turns something over in his heart
f-w-j as a single semantic idea: gathering, coming together in a mass
From this comes fawj, a group or band of people.
h-m-n (هـ-م-ن) is not a real root at all — it carries no established meaning of its own
highlights.note: Ibn Fāris: no root of its own

highlights.text: al-muhaymin (المهيمن), "the witness" (al-shāhid)
One core meaning: the faintness of a sound or sensation.
al-hams — a faint sound; hams al-aqdām — the faintest possible tread of a footstep.
a single core meaning: the neck
jīd = "neck"; plural ajyād.
in a line by the poet al-Aʿshā, "the men of Iyād bi-ajyādihā,"
Its only content is مدينة (madīna), "city, town"
the plural is مُدُن (mudun, "cities")
the root م و ل (m-w-l) carries a single notion, tied to wealth or property (māl)
تَمَوَّلَ (tamawwala) means "the man acquired wealth/property,"
from a single core idea: a sound or cry (ṣawt)
naʿaqa al-rāʿī bi-l-ghanam — "the shepherd naʿaqa at the sheep" — meaning the shepherd shouted or cried out
**al-nūn (النُّون)** — "the fish" / "the whale."
a single root whose core meaning is waiting and expectation
The derived form التَّرَبُّص (tarabbuṣ) means "awaiting," as in تَرَبَّصْتُ بِهِ ("I waited for him")
a single core meaning: firmness, being firmly fixed or established
Anything called رَاسِخ (rāsikh, "deeply-rooted, firmly fixed")
to make a liquid flow/pour out
safaka damahu — "he shed/poured out his blood," i.e., caused it to flow.
s-w-gh as the easy going-down of a drink
The Qur'an has "easy to swallow (sāʾigh) for those who drink" (Q 16:66)
the root t-r-q yields only a single word: tarquwa, "collarbone" (clavicle)
core meaning: returning / turning back (rujūʿ)
تَابَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ means "he turned back from his sin"
One core meaning: al-wahaj — the heat of fire and its blazing.
sirāj wahhāj — a blazing lamp
To strike with a clenched fist — literally, with the gathered/closed hand (ضربه بجمع كفه, ḍarabahu bi-jumʿi kaffihi).
a single root meaning the opposite of "good/wholesome" (al-ṭayyib)
خَبِيث (khabīth) — "vile, foul; not good."
a single, regular root with one core meaning: the purifying and refining of a thing
intransitive: خَلَصَ ("it became pure/clear/free")
single root whose core sense is deficiency or loss (al-naqṣ)
خَسَرْتُ الْمِيزَانَ and أَخْسَرْتُهُ mean "I made the balance deficient"
core meaning is entering into the middle of something and penetrating it
"they entered together into the discourse and the matter,"
the attachment of one thing to another
one falsely/illegitimately attached to a lineage
a line of poetry describing a zanīm as one "added on" by men
